label: Лишь
description: A 10-sentence usage card for лишь (only, merely), a bookish restrictive adverb.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Bookish only. 'Лишь' means only or merely, a more literary equivalent of только. Before 'хотел' it softens the verb to merely wanted to ask, downplaying the intent.
Strategic focus: Restricting the subject. Placing 'лишь' before 'она' focuses on the subject, meaning only she and no one else understood. Position decides what the restriction targets.
Strategic focus: Restricting a small quantity. 'Лишь' before 'несколько минут' stresses only a few minutes are left. The adverb narrows focus to that phrase and emphasises how little remains.
Strategic focus: Merely the start. 'Лишь' before 'начало' means just the beginning, minimising the noun. The adverb gives a refined, literary tone compared with только.
Strategic focus: Restricting the action. 'Лишь' before 'кивал' focuses on the verb, meaning he did nothing but nod. The adverb narrows the whole behaviour to that single action.
Strategic focus: Restricting time. 'Лишь' before 'сейчас' means only now, stressing how late the understanding came. The adverb focuses on the time word and carries a bookish flavour.
Strategic focus: Лишь бы as if only. The fixed phrase 'лишь бы' expresses a wish, meaning if only everything goes well. This optative use is distinct from the plain restrictive only.
Strategic focus: Restricting the cause. 'Лишь' before 'чудо' means only a miracle saved us, focusing on the single reason. The adverb singles out the noun in a literary, dramatic way.
Strategic focus: Merely a gesture. 'Лишь' before 'улыбнулась' means she merely smiled and did no more. The adverb restricts the response to that one quiet reaction.

missions.phrase: В комнате горела лишь одна свеча.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Restricting to a single thing. 'Лишь' before 'одна свеча' stresses that only one candle was burning. The adverb narrows focus to that lone object in a vivid, literary scene.
